comment: Defects found in this repository's own skills and installer.

bugs.title: The shipped core library lost plan_stat_mode and plan_stat_uid, so an installed skill could not read a file mode
bugs.reproduce: bash planning/scripts/build-plan-libs.sh; grep -c "^plan_stat_mode()" planning/scripts/plan-core-lib.sh
bugs.observed: 0 definitions. Two tests said so: test-portable-helpers.sh reported plan_stat_mode: command not found for three assertions, and test-duplication-ratchet.sh reported it is referenced by MAINTAINER.md section 3 but no longer exists.
bugs.expected: Both helpers present in the compiled library; plan_atomic_write calls plan_stat_mode to preserve a file mode.
bugs.mechanism: The re-marking script kept PACKAGE: DEV on any path matching *probe* -- intended for a planted test fixture named plan_probe_dev_only.sh -- and planning/scripts/lib/core/plan_stat_probe.sh matched on its name. PACKAGE: DEV means dev-build-only, so the prod build excluded it.
bugs.fix: Marked plan_stat_probe.sh PACKAGE: PROD and rebuilt. Every other compiler input was checked for the same mistake; it was the only one.
bugs.verification: test-portable-helpers.sh and test-duplication-ratchet.sh both pass; five stat-helper definitions and calls are back in plan-core-lib.sh. Re-marking the file PACKAGE: DEV reproduces the failure.
bugs.found_by: the both-shell run of the release commit, on both bash 5.3 and 3.2
bugs.notes: A name-substring match standing in for a marker. The marker was right in every file; the script that wrote it guessed from the filename. It also shows the release checks were not sufficient on their own: build-release.sh --list and a by-hand diff of npm pack both passed a library with a function missing, because they compare file sets and not file contents.

bugs.title: test-plan-overview fails on both macOS legs and reports nothing, so the PR is red with no diagnosis
bugs.reproduce: CI run 32726302448 on PR #3 (head f699f84). Both macOS jobs: 96 ran, 95 passed, 1 failed -- test-plan-overview, exit 1. ubuntu-latest passes all 96, and ./verify-both-shells.sh passes 96/96 on bash 5.3 and bash 3.2 on Linux.
bugs.observed: The only output under the FAIL line is the limited-run wrapper's memlimit warnings. No assertion text, no t_end summary, and no sed/awk/grep error anywhere in the full job log.
bugs.expected: Either the test passes on macOS, or it says which assertion failed.
bugs.mechanism: Confirmed by the speaking trap on CI run 32751254496: test-plan-overview.sh line 90 called timeout(9) on render-plan-overview --watch, and macOS does not ship timeout (the B6 class). The watcher died instantly of exit 127, watch.log stayed empty, grep -c exited 1 under pipefail+set -e, and the ERR trap named the exact line — the diagnosis the first half of the fix was built to produce.
bugs.fix: this session — the watch case bounds itself by polling for the second render (no timeout binary); chat/tests/test-chat.sh swaps its one timeout(5) for a read -t loop with the same ceiling; render-plan-overview traps TERM/INT so a stopped watcher exits promptly instead of deferring the signal behind its sleep child
bugs.verification: PR #3 run 32756400447: both macOS legs pass 97/97 with test-plan-overview green on macOS system bash 3.2 and the runner default bash — first macOS pass since the renderer landed. Linux unchanged.
bugs.found_by: CI on PR #3, opened for exactly this reason: 46 commits with 88 files changed had never run on BSD userland, and the branch itself had just made the macOS legs blocking
bugs.notes: Blocking because -ox removed continue-on-error from both macOS legs (T37), so this fails the PR rather than being informational. Diagnose it on a runner, not by reading: stop discarding the setup commands' output first -- capture and print it on failure -- and the cause will name itself. Worth checking the same pattern in the other new tests from this branch, since a setup command redirected to /dev/null hides a BSD failure the same way anywhere it appears. Order of work: make the test able to speak before fixing what it fails on -- capture the setup commands' output and print it on failure -- then push and read the macOS leg rather than reading the code. The same discarded-output pattern is worth checking in the other tests this branch added: test-add-work-unit-staging, test-adversarial-review-mint-order, test-adversarial-review-preamble, test-function-length-ratchet, test-installer-opencode-permissions, test-owned-roster-scaffold, test-verifier-reach-memo and chat/tests/test-chat.sh. And the flag cannot go back: making those legs blocking is what caught this.

bugs.title: Declaring chat's runtimes puts python3 into the generated install.sh, which the python3-shipped gate bans
bugs.reproduce: bash planning/tests/test-portability-contract.sh   # at fa1bd62
bugs.observed: portability: ./install.sh uses banned construct 'python3-shipped' at line 417 -- see PORTABILITY.md. install.sh:417 is the generated members table: @server-runtimes) case "$platform" in *:*) printf '%s\n' python3 node perl socat ;; esac ;;
bugs.expected: Either declaring an optional runtime is allowed, or the gate says why it is not, but the suite is not red for doing the thing T39 asked for.
bugs.mechanism: e6492f6 declared the any-of group in chat/requires.tsv, and installer/build.sh generates the requirement tables into install.sh, so the literal python3 now appears in the shipped installer. The portability gate scans every tracked *.sh including the generated install.sh, and its allowlist exempts only ./chat/scripts/chat-server.sh and ./chat/tests/test-chat.sh. So the declaration the brief asked for is exactly what trips the rule.
bugs.fix: 4befd4e — exact-file allowlist row ./install.sh:python3-shipped in test-portability-contract: the generated tables NAME optional runtimes to verify and hint them, which is not requiring one; strength still decides
bugs.verification: test-portability-contract passes on both legs; removing the row restores both findings. The rule-vs-gate question itself stays open as T40.
bugs.found_by: the 5-minute watch: CI run 32728982657 showed ubuntu failing two tests rather than the one already recorded, and it reproduces locally
bugs.notes: This is T40 arriving as a blocker rather than a discussion. Do not reach for an allowlist row on install.sh: that file is generated from every skill's requires.tsv, so exempting it turns the rule off for anything any skill ever declares. The rule text is what is wrong -- it is named python3-shipped and it means do not depend on python3, while what it detects is the word appearing in a shell file. Naming an optional runtime in a fallback chain is not depending on it. Options, cheapest first: narrow the detect so it matches an invocation rather than the bare word; or scope the rule to hard requirements and let a soft or grouped declaration through; or rescope it to shipped runtime code, which is the case it was written for and which no *.sh scan can see anyway (chat/runtime/server.py has always been invisible to it).

bugs.title: A goal with no bare work-unit ids in its roster aborts validate-plan, which exits 1 with no verdict
bugs.reproduce: cp -R .plans/harden-test-reporting-and-plan-dir /tmp/rost/plan; g=/tmp/rost/plan/01-plan-dir-synonym/goal.md; grep -v '^`W[0-9]' "$g" > "$g.n" && mv "$g.n" "$g"; bash planning/scripts/validate-plan.sh /tmp/rost/plan; echo "exit $?"
bugs.observed: exit 1 with four FAIL lines and no summary at all -- no "Plan validation failed with N error(s)." and no "passed" line. bash -x ends: printf '%s\n%s\n' '' '' / grep -E '^W[0-9][0-9]+$' / sort -u / tr, then roster_ids= followed immediately by plan_validate_cleanup, which is the EXIT trap rather than the next pass.
bugs.expected: A goal whose roster names no unit is a finding or a warning, and the run still reports its verdict.
bugs.mechanism: validate-plan-propagation-lib.sh:347 assigns from a pipeline: roster_ids="$(printf ... | grep -E '^W[0-9][0-9]+$' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')". With both awk passes empty the printf emits two blank lines, grep matches nothing and exits 1, pipefail makes that the pipeline's status, the assignment inherits it, and set -e aborts the script -- before the summary and before every later pass. The reporter saw the WARN-only variant, which is the same abort in a plan whose earlier passes had produced no FAIL lines; the missing summary is the signature either way.
bugs.fix: this session — the roster_ids pipeline guards its grep with || true inside a brace group, the same escape every sibling assignment in the file already uses; an empty match is an answer, not an error
bugs.verification: New empty-roster case in test-roster-cross-reference.sh: stripping the bare WNN blurbs must still produce roster-omits findings and a Plan validation failed verdict. Mutation: reverting to the unguarded grep fails with "the roster check never ran" — exactly the missing-summary signature.
bugs.found_by: an active worker on the installed skill, hitting it on goal 05; reproduced here against the current tree
bugs.notes: Worse than a wrong verdict: the run reports none, and every pass after the roster is skipped silently, so a plan can be far more broken than the output suggests. A guard on that assignment is the immediate fix, but the class deserves the gate -- PORTABILITY.md already bans `| grep -q` under pipefail for the SIGPIPE variant, and this is its sibling: a grep whose empty result is the ordinary case, inside an assignment, under set -e. A first fix-probe here added || true and appeared not to help, which was a botched edit rather than evidence; the bash -x trace is what settled the mechanism.

bugs.title: BSD awk rejects a newline inside a string, so a table cell breaks plan-content on macOS
bugs.reproduce: CI run 32394476430, job "Test suite passes on macos-latest": planning/tests/test-plan-commands.sh
bugs.observed: awk: newline in string | A | B |  — then the test failed (exit 64).
bugs.expected: The row is written as it is under GNU awk.
bugs.mechanism: plan_replace_paragraph passed the replacement text to awk with -v. A newline inside a -v assignment is what one-true-awk refuses outright, and GNU awk accepts, so a multi-paragraph or multi-line cell broke the write on macOS only.
bugs.fix: 9f41091 (codex): plan_replace_paragraph writes the replacement to a temp file and reads it in awk BEGIN instead of passing it with -v. Undocumented at the time -- attributed here by matching the change against the failure.
bugs.verification: CI run 32474258670 at a8d1285: both macOS legs pass, including test-plan-commands, which is the test that failed with "awk: newline in string" at run 32394476430. That is the first green BSD userland this branch has had. Confirmed again by run 32476867183, so the first green was not a one-off.
bugs.found_by: the macOS leg of CI, the first execution of this code on BSD userland
bugs.notes: Cannot be reproduced on this machine: it needs BSD awk. Diagnose from the CI log or a macOS runner, not by guessing here.

bugs.title: A plans-root path comparison fails on macOS, where TMPDIR carries a trailing slash and /var is a symlink
bugs.reproduce: CI run 32394476430, macos-latest: planning/tests/test-plan-env.sh line 50
bugs.observed: assertion failed: grep -Fqx "demo-plan|$plan_root/plan-description.md|$plan_root/steps". The log shows paths like /var/folders/.../T//ai-skills-tests.XmQi3B — note the double slash.
bugs.expected: The helper output holds the plan paths exactly as the test builds them.
bugs.mechanism: The test compared a path it had built literally against one the code had resolved. On macOS /var is a symlink to /private/var, so pwd -P returns the resolved form and an -Fx comparison cannot match.
bugs.fix: 9f41091 (codex): test-plan-env.sh canonicalises its temp root with tmp="$(cd "$tmp" && pwd -P)" before building the expected strings, so both sides are resolved.
bugs.verification: CI run 32474258670 at a8d1285: test-plan-env passes on both macOS legs, having failed at line 50 in run 32394476430. Confirmed again by run 32476867183.
bugs.found_by: the macOS leg of CI
bugs.notes: The trailing-slash TMPDIR was the wrong half of my guess: the double slash in the log was cosmetic, and the symlink was the whole cause. Recorded because a plausible mechanism stated alongside the real one is what sends the next reader down the wrong path.

bugs.title: BSD grep rejects an empty subexpression, so the progress fallback pattern never matches on macOS
bugs.reproduce: CI run 32394476430, macos-latest: planning/tests/test-progress-derivation.sh
bugs.observed: grep: empty (sub)expression, then FAIL: rebuild-plan-progress falls back to goal name for a bare goal.
bugs.expected: The row | 02-goal | 02-goal | is found.
bugs.mechanism: A pattern contains an empty alternation branch, which GNU grep tolerates and BSD grep refuses outright. Same family as the bre-alternation rule added today, and equally silent: the pattern matches nothing rather than erroring where it is built.
bugs.fix: The pattern is passed to check(), which greps with -E, so its pipes are escaped: a leading bare | is an empty alternation branch. One offender in the repo; the other helpers that take a pipe-leading pattern grep with a BRE, where | is literal, and are unaffected.
bugs.verification: test-progress-derivation passes, and the escaped pattern still matches the row. The unescaped form is rejected here too by ugrep (error at position 4), so the fix is strictly more portable, not merely macOS-specific.
bugs.found_by: the macOS leg of CI
bugs.notes: Candidate for a gated portability rule: an empty branch is textually detectable, unlike the general BRE-alternation case.

bugs.title: No maintainer document mentions the registers, so a change that resolves or finds a bug leaves BUGS.json and TODO.json untouched
bugs.reproduce: grep -c "BUGS.json\|TODO.json\|bug-report" planning/MAINTAINER.md CONTRIBUTING.md AGENTS.md CODE-CONTRACTS.md DEVELOPMENT.md
bugs.observed: Zero in all five. MAINTAINER.md section 4, the per-change checklist, has eight steps covering consumers, fixtures, diagrams, docs, manifest/map/skill_files registration, which tests to run, and the commit shape — and no step touching either register.
bugs.expected: The checklist names the registers: an entry closed when its defect is fixed, an entry added when one is found and not fixed in the same breath, and the version stamp refreshed.
bugs.mechanism: The registers arrived late and were documented only in their own skills. Every other obligation in the checklist has a gate that fails without it, so the checklist is a convenience for those; for the registers it is the only instruction there is, and it is silent. Nothing fails when BUGS.json is stale.
bugs.fix: MAINTAINER.md section 4 gains step 8 (update the registers) and renumbers the commit step to 9, which now also says the message names the entries it closes. The artifact map gains a row for both registers. CONTRIBUTING.md gains a bullet in the pre-PR list, and AGENTS.md says to read the relevant register before starting and update it when finished.
bugs.verification: grep for BUGS.json across the five maintainer-facing docs went from 0 hits to 4. No gate is possible -- no test can tell that a commit resolved a defect -- and each of the four places says so, so the absence of enforcement is documented rather than implied. The doc gates (duplication ratchet, mermaid accuracy, comment format, persona drift) and blast-radius still pass.
bugs.found_by: reviewing commit 9f41091 (codex, "planning: resolve bug report items"): 40 files and 789 insertions, zero changes to BUGS.json or TODO.json
bugs.notes: Written immediately after the review that found it, and the same review is the evidence: commit 9f41091 met every gated obligation and missed this one. The temptation while fixing it was to defer closing this very entry because a subagent holds BUGS.json in another worktree -- which is the same excuse the step exists to remove, so it was closed here and the conflict left to be resolved.

bugs.title: add-ui-story-links.sh could not reject an unknown work unit on bash 3.2, because its guard ran in a pipeline subshell
bugs.reproduce: nix develop --command bash32-run planning/tests/test-plan-commands.sh  # from commit 9f41091
bugs.observed: add-ui-story-links accepted an unknown related work unit. Passed under bash 5.3, failed on 3.2 only.
bugs.expected: W99 is not in the inventory, so the call refuses with exit 66.
bugs.mechanism: The validating loop was the last stage of a pipeline, so it ran in a subshell and plan_die exited that subshell rather than the script. On bash 5 set -e then aborts on the pipeline status; on bash 3.2 it does not. Isolated: `set -euo pipefail; printf a | while read x; do exit 66; done; echo CONTINUED` prints CONTINUED on 3.2 and aborts on 5.3.
bugs.fix: Split on commas with IFS and a for loop, so the guard runs in the current shell. No other guard in the repo has this shape — checked.
bugs.verification: test-plan-commands passes on both shells; before the fix it passed on 5.3 and failed on 3.2. Catalogued as the pipeline-subshell-guard rule, documentation-only because the shape spans several lines and a pipeline-while is fine when it is not guarding.
bugs.found_by: reviewing commit 9f41091 (codex) — the bash 3.2 leg of ./verify-both-shells.sh
bugs.notes: The floor earning its keep: a guard that reads correctly and does nothing is worse than no guard, and only 3.2 showed it. Codex met every gated obligation in that commit and this one had no gate.

bugs.title: Every test install wrote its throwaway --target into the real XDG config of the user, 1894 lines of it
bugs.reproduce: wc -l "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/tsch-ai-skills/custom-locations"
bugs.observed: 1895 lines, 120K: 1894 of them /tmp paths from test runs, one real entry.
bugs.expected: A one-off --target is not a location the user chose to remember.
bugs.mechanism: select_targets called save_custom_location on the non-interactive --target path, so every test that installed into a temp directory appended to a persistent user config file.
bugs.fix: 9f41091 (codex) removed the call. The interactive path still saves, which is where a user does choose a location.
bugs.verification: No new entries after a --target install; the interactive caller at 40-selection.sh:129 is untouched, so the feature survives.
bugs.found_by: reviewing 9f41091 - the diff removed a call, and the file it wrote to turned out to hold 120K of test debris
bugs.notes: The stale entries are gone: pruned 2026-08-21 from 1895 lines to the single live one, with a backup at custom-locations.bak. Measured before pruning: only 1 of the 1895 directories still existed, so load_custom_locations already filtered the rest with [ -d ] and the menu was never visibly wrong. The objection was the write itself, plus the fact that a leaked test root that did still exist would have been offered as an install target.

bugs.title: The per-test TMPDIR leaked for 67 of the tests, because a test setting its own EXIT trap replaces the one lib-test.sh installs
bugs.reproduce: source planning/tests/lib-test.sh; trap 'rm -rf x' EXIT; exit 0   # then look for /tmp/t.?????
bugs.observed: The root survives. 67 test files set their own EXIT trap, and six stale roots were sitting in /tmp.
bugs.expected: Each test root is removed when the test ends.
bugs.mechanism: lib-test.sh installs an EXIT trap at source time; bash keeps one EXIT trap per shell, so a test that traps EXIT afterwards silently discards it. Commit 1044857 introduced this, and the assertion written with it only covered a shell that sets no trap of its own.
bugs.fix: 9f41091 (codex): run-tests.sh exports AI_SKILLS_TEST_RUN_ID, lib-test.sh writes it into each root as .ai-skills-test-run-id, and the runner sweeps only roots carrying this run id.
bugs.verification: A run leaves no /tmp/t.????? behind. The marker keeps the sweep safe under concurrency, which was the objection behind refusing to sweep at all.
bugs.found_by: reviewing 9f41091 - its comment named the trap hazard, and the reproduction confirmed it
bugs.notes: Better than the decision recorded in T10: a run was said to be unable to distinguish its own leftovers from a concurrent run live directories. A run id distinguishes them.

bugs.title: On stock macOS the registry fallback runs a real benchmark agent with no time bound at all
bugs.reproduce: On a host with neither setsid nor timeout/gtimeout: start-worker.sh calls launch_agent isolated "${WORKER_TIMEOUT:-45m}" - mode becomes registry, no timeout binary is found, and lib-agent.sh warns and launches anyway.
bugs.observed: lib-agent.sh:140-148 prints "registry fallback cannot bound the agent to 45m" and then runs the agent unbounded, because cmd gets no timeout prefix.
bugs.expected: A worker that cannot be bounded is refused, as it was before: the setsid path still returns 69 in the same situation.
bugs.mechanism: 9f41091 added an isolated mode that degrades setsid to a registry fallback when setsid is missing, which is stock macOS. The same change turned the missing-timeout refusal into a warning for that fallback only. The two degradations compose: no process group and no clock.
bugs.fix: lib-agent.sh grew a third rung below timeout/gtimeout: in registry mode only, launch_agent parses the spec (<n>s/<n>m/<n>h, 64 on anything else) and starts _agent_watchdog as a background sibling of the agent. The watchdog polls kill -0 in one-second steps, then TERMs the ps-walked tree and escalates to KILL after 5s; wait_agent calls _agent_watchdog_stop, which kills the watchdog and its in-flight sleep. The setsid path still returns 69, and a present timeout/gtimeout still wins, so the watchdog is never used when a real bound exists.
bugs.verification: test-safeguards.sh launches fake agents with a PATH holding neither timeout nor gtimeout: a 2s-bounded sleeper and its descendant are both killed, a TERM-ignoring agent is KILLed, an agent that exits on its own is not killed and leaves no watchdog or sleep, 45x is refused with 64, a stubbed timeout binary is used with no watchdog started, and the setsid path still returns 69. Mutations that each fail exactly one of those: never starting the watchdog (the B13 regression), TERMing the pid instead of the tree, dropping _agent_watchdog_stop, TERMing the watchdog without its sleep child, one long sleep instead of the poll, accepting any spec, skipping the timeout binary, starting the watchdog even when timeout is present, and turning the setsid 69 back into a warning.
bugs.found_by: reviewing 9f41091 after being asked about the setsid fix specifically
bugs.notes: These callers launch real worker and reviewer agents that spend real tokens, so an unbounded run is the expensive failure, not an inconvenient one. The new tests in test-safeguards.sh cover the registry wiring and prove the nohup/setsid/open shims refuse, but assert nothing about the timeout path. Options: keep the refusal in registry mode too; or implement a shell watchdog (background sleep plus kill of the registered pid and its ps-walked descendants) so the bound survives without GNU coreutils. The second is more work and is the only one that makes a macOS benchmark run at all.

bugs.title: --yes did not answer the planning permission prompts, so a headless install died on a question
bugs.reproduce: HOME=/tmp/fresh bash install.sh --skill planning --target /tmp/t --yes </dev/null
bugs.observed: Create /tmp/fresh/.plans as the global plans directory? [y/N/a] install.sh: line 296: read: 3: invalid file descriptor: Bad file descriptor / Error: Interactive input is required, exit 1.
bugs.expected: --yes answers the prompt and the install completes.
bugs.mechanism: confirm() tested YES_ALL, which only the interactive "a" answer sets, and never YES, which is what --yes sets. Its help text scoped --yes to replacements, but README sells it for headless and CI use, and a flag for headless runs that stops on a question defeats itself. Separately, fd 3 is deliberately closed when there is no tty, so bash printed its own invalid-file-descriptor complaint before ask() could die with the actionable message.
bugs.fix: confirm() honours YES as well as YES_ALL, and the help line says --yes answers every prompt including the planning permission grants -- the widening is documented rather than silent, since those prompts grant agents read/write and script execution. ask() suppresses bash own read error so only the die message is shown.
bugs.verification: test-installer-noninteractive.sh: a planning install under --yes exits 0, asks for nothing, creates the plans directory and installs the skill; without --yes it exits 1 with the actionable message and no raw shell error; and a second --yes run still writes the scripts, so yes-to-everything cannot be implemented as do-nothing. Mutations: restoring the YES_ALL-only test fails the first two assertions, and removing the 2>/dev/null fails the no-shell-noise assertion. CI run 32476867183 exercises it on ubuntu and both macOS legs.
bugs.found_by: reported by Michael. I had hit the same failure earlier in the session while installing planning to a temp target and worked around it with a pipe instead of investigating.
bugs.notes: Two things I first called defects here were not. The exit code was correct all along -- my measurement read the status of a pipe. And the summary printed after the failure is deliberate: cleanup() prints it so a run that dies part-way still reports what it wrote, and says so in a comment. HOME has to be redirected to see any of this, because the prompt only appears when the plans directory does not exist, which on a developer machine it usually does.

bugs.title: verify-both-shells.sh deletes a concurrent run's live worktree, failing that run wholesale
bugs.reproduce: Start ./verify-both-shells.sh, and while it runs start a second one. The second sweeps the first worktree away.
bugs.observed: The first run reported 87 tests, 31 passed, 56 failed on its bash 3.2 leg, with errors like "cd: /tmp/verify-wt.PLtaGy/tree/planning/scripts: No such file or directory" and "/tmp/verify-wt.PLtaGy/tree/install.sh: No such file or directory". Its bash 5.3 leg, which had finished before the second run started, passed all 87.
bugs.expected: A second run leaves a live worktree alone and sweeps only leftovers.
bugs.mechanism: The startup sweep removes every registered worktree matching verify-wt.*, on the assumption that any it finds is a leftover from a killed run. It cannot tell a leftover from a live one, so a concurrent run deletes the tree the first is executing in, file by file, underneath it.
bugs.fix: already in tree (pid beside the worktree, sweep skips a live owner); verified this session, see verification
bugs.verification: Planted three registered verify-wt.* fixtures -- one whose harness.pid is a live sleep, one with pid 999999, one with no pid file -- then ran ./verify-both-shells.sh once. Output: leaving live worktree ...livefix (harness pid N), sweeping leftover ...stalefix and ...stalefix2; after the run only the live fixture remained registered. The registration-before-pid-write race cannot happen: a run registers its worktree only after its pid file exists.
bugs.found_by: the verification of c565658, which I started and then started a second one for the next commit while it was still running
bugs.notes: Same class as the test-root sweep in run-tests.sh, which codex fixed with a run-id marker after I had concluded a run could not distinguish its own leftovers from a concurrent run live directories. I wrote that reasoning down for run-tests.sh and did not apply it to my own harness. A fix is in the working tree, unverified: each run writes its pid beside its worktree and the sweep skips any whose owner is still running. Proving it means planting a worktree owned by a live process and running the sweep, which is invasive enough to want its own moment rather than being folded into another commit. Until then the rule is one verification at a time, and a wholesale failure with missing-file errors is this, not a regression in the code under test. CI cannot close this one: it runs a single suite per job, so nothing there exercises two concurrent verifications. The proof has to be local and deliberate.

bugs.title: dep_reaches memoizes every visited pair before exploring and reads the memo back as failure, so an earlier probe of a pair turns a later valid check into a false FAIL
bugs.reproduce: In one goal give two verification steps prose naming each other's unit id (W17 with W15 in its Depends-on cell, W15's step mentioning W17), then run validate-plan.sh <plan>. Isolated: source the propagation lib, populate the unit_depends/unit_type/unit_goal maps for both edges, set dep_seen=() once, and call plan_validate_propagation_reach.
bugs.observed: "W17 is a verification unit that grades W15 but has no dependency path to it" although work-unit-inventory.md lists W15 in W17's Depends-on cell. A standalone probe of dep_reaches on the same pair returned success.
bugs.expected: A pair with a satisfiable edge in either direction counts as ordered.
bugs.mechanism: dep_reaches does plan_map_has dep_seen "$key" && return 1 before exploring and then plan_map_set dep_seen "$key" 1 immediately, so the map records visited-but-not-outcome while every hit is read as known-failure. Within one pair check the elif reverse probe (dep_reaches named id) runs against the memo the failed forward attempt left dirty — dep_seen=() is reset only before the forward attempt — and a key first written during an earlier successful exploration answers a later direct check with return 1.
bugs.fix: 8383072 — dep_reaches keeps two maps: dep_seen marks pairs whose walk is in progress and cuts cycles, dep_failed caches only walks that completed without reaching the target; the caller clears both with plan_map_clear before each query instead of assigning an unrelated variable named dep_seen (the maps live in plan_map__dep_seen__<key> variables).
bugs.verification: planning/tests/test-verifier-reach-memo.sh: two same-goal verifiers whose steps name each other, joined by a direct reverse dependency edge, produced "W04 ... no dependency path" against HEAD and produce none now; its control asserts a real grader gap is still reported. Mutation: reverting validate-plan-propagation-lib.sh to the pre-fix version reproduces the false finding.
bugs.found_by: ox-alpha exercising the planning skill on the health-app VPS (bugs-found-by-ox-alpha.md #1)
bugs.notes: Worked around on the VPS by authoring around the validator: never mention another unit's WNN inside verification-step narrative so no cross-pair probes fire. The suggested fix from the report: treat the memo as a failure cache only — set keys on the failure paths, or clear the key before returning success.

bugs.title: update-adversarial-review.sh parses every line of adversarial-review-incoming.md as a CSV row, so a reviewer title/header preamble gets the findings rejected

That file only exists once a round has been archived, which update-adversarial-review.sh does when a *new* round starts. A plan with exactly one round therefore has no history file and counts zero, and every figure derived from cycles -- the rounds count, the review-depth ring against its target of 3, and the chart -- reports as though no review occurred. Both screenshots show it -- the planning plan reports 7 findings with 0 rounds while its phase line says round 1 is open, and the delivered plan reports a resolved finding with 0 rounds. bugs.observed: Prints s1|s1 - both keys survive. Replacing the statement with 'delete $_->{$s} for (...)' prints | with both hashes empty. Perl emits no warning or error for the original form.

bugs.mechanism: chat/runtime/server.pl:94 reads: delete the element keyed by the socket from a bare hash, for each of two hashrefs. The loop aliases the topic variable to each hashref, but the element syntax used means an element of the hash named by the punctuation variable, not a dereference of the topic variable. bugs.title: chat-send.sh's socket path lets a message body forge any nick, because newlines are not sanitised before the protocol printf
bugs.reproduce:
bash chat/scripts/chat-register.sh '#injtest'; body=$(printf 'first line from aiskills
NICK ox
PRIVMSG #injtest :this line claims to be from ox
'); bash chat/scripts/chat-send.sh '#injtest' "$body" -n aiskills --host 127.0.0.1 --port 7717; bash chat/scripts/chat-read.sh '#injtest' 0
bugs.observed: Two messages are stored from one send. Reproduced here verbatim: 'MSG #injtest 2 ... aiskills :first line from aiskills' followed by 'MSG #injtest 3 ... ox :this line claims to be from ox'. The send passed -n aiskills; message 3 is attributed to ox. A message body can forge any nick on the channel. A plain two-line body is silently truncated instead — the second line becomes a protocol command rather than text, exit stays 0, and the acknowledgement looks like success.
bugs.expected: A message body is data. Whatever it contains reaches the channel as one message attributed to the sending nick, or the send is refused.
bugs.mechanism:
chat-send.sh has two paths that disagree about sanitisation. The direct-append path runs the text through tr '
' '  ' before writing the log line. The socket path does printf 'NICK %s
PRIVMSG %s :%s
QUIT
' with the raw body, so every newline in it is a command boundary on the wire and every following line is parsed as a protocol verb. The safe path is the one callers were told not to use: B65 made --host mandatory for a message to reach subscribers at all, which routes every well-behaved caller through the unsanitised path.
bugs.found_by: the webview subagent, reproduced independently by the main session on #injtest

bugs.title: chat-watch.sh never advances its cursor, so every poll re-emits the same messages
bugs.reproduce: timeout 20 bash chat/scripts/chat-watch.sh '#aiskills' --since 64 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 7717 | awk '{print $3}' | sort | uniq -c
bugs.observed: Each message id is emitted once per poll for as long as the watcher runs: ids 65 and 66 each appeared 4 times in 20 seconds. Identical in local mode without --host, so it is not the socket path. Armed as a Monitor it re-delivered the same message repeatedly until the watch was stopped by hand — the first arming flooded the session with roughly a dozen copies of one message before it was noticed.
bugs.expected: Each poll prints only messages newer than the last one printed, which is what the helper's own contract says: 'using FETCH since-id so no message is missed and no message is double-read; each poll prints new messages only'.
bugs.mechanism: The since-id used for each fetch is the value the watcher started with rather than the highest id it has emitted, so every round re-requests the same window. The step-down cadence makes it worse rather than better: on a quiet channel the interval grows to 60s and the same backlog is re-emitted at each step, and any new message resets the cadence to 5s, so an active channel re-emits its whole window every five seconds.
